response.internal_assessment: The number I have been trying not to say out loud is now on the table: I am unemployed. That word is not supposed to apply to me. I built this company. My father started it. And somewhere between the executive meeting with Rick and the layoffs I authorized, the formal status shifted. The savings are still substantial — $412,000, roughly 25 months at current burn — but $0 monthly income means every month that passes is a month I cannot get back. The sector revenue index is at 79. Foot traffic at Millfield Auto Mall is down 14%. Test-drive conversion fell from 31% to 22%. Those numbers are not a blip. That is a structural drop. Rick told me what I needed to hear: service lane at 79% utilization is the one thing still working. I need to reorganize around that truth and stop pretending the showroom will recover on its own. The layoffs I made — I carry those. Some of those people worked for my father. I owe them more than a clean separation. Angela Wright is moving on the transition plan. Maria Santos is running public listening sessions, pushing RoboRide compliance, and expanding small business grants. The community apparatus is moving. I need to move too — not reactively, but with a plan I can actually execute from my current position, which is: no income, shrinking business footprint, and a legacy institution that may need to become something smaller and more durable than what I built.
response.inbox_interpretation: Rick Tanner has walked into the meeting prepared. He brought unfiltered data — foot traffic down 14%, conversion rate collapsed, service lane holding. He committed to producing a location-specific consolidation readiness assessment within two weeks and framed it as an asset map, not a layoff list. That framing is mine — I gave him the three-tier framework and he used it correctly. He is telling me he wants to manage the transition and stay. I hear that. Angela Wright is signaling progress on the workforce transition plan and has sent a formal update. Maria Santos is acting: listening session, RoboRide compliance enforcement, grant expansion using Betty Kowalski's testimony. The city is not ignoring this. The 'unemployed' outcome from tick 5 is the system registering that I laid off workers including, it appears, myself in some formal sense — or that the business structure has changed enough that my prior employment category no longer holds. Either way, I cannot draw a CEO salary from a company that is actively restructuring and bleeding revenue. That was probably the right call even if the system made it before I did.

chosen_actions.description: Formally accept Rick Tanner's two-week timeline for the Millfield Auto Mall consolidation readiness assessment. Confirm in writing that his three-tier asset map — not a layoff list — is the authoritative document I will use for any Q2 consolidation decisions. Signal to him directly that the service lane is the survival core and that I will not make staffing decisions that undercut certified technician capacity. This is the strategic pivot I have been building toward: from a four-location sales-volume model to a service-and-retention model built around the parts of the business that autonomous ride-share cannot touch.

resources.detail: Delegating the consolidation readiness assessment to Rick Tanner. No cash transfer. Granting him the authority to frame the Q2 plan.

chosen_actions.reasoning: Rick's data is clear and his framing is sound. The service lane is at 79% utilization — that is the moat. Confirming his authority to produce the asset map locks in the strategic direction before anyone else — including me — second-guesses it under pressure.

chosen_actions.description: Write private notes — not for distribution, not for HR files — about each person laid off this month. Document their role, their tenure, what they contributed to the business my father started, and what I can realistically do for them: a direct call to Howard Liu at the parts store, a strong written reference, a referral into Angela's transition program, or outplacement support through the Maria Santos task force channels now that the grant threshold is being lowered to 10% for auto row businesses. I will not manage the narrative on this. I will sit with what I did.
chosen_actions.reasoning: These were people. Some of them knew my father. Managing the narrative without first sitting with the human cost would be a failure of character, not just leadership. I need to do this before I can lead anything else with credibility.

chosen_actions.description: Begin restructuring my own compensation and formal role. I am currently drawing no income and listed as unemployed. Rather than treating this as a crisis to be reversed, I will formalize a reduced operational role — not CEO in the traditional sense, but owner-operator focused on the restructuring process. This means: no salary draw until the business has a functional Q2 plan, personal expenses managed against savings, and a clear 90-day horizon to either restore income through the restructured service-lane model or begin exploring whether the brand and assets should be partially sold or consolidated with another operator. I will not pretend I can afford to keep all four locations running at current overhead. That decision is coming. I need to be the one who makes it, not the one it happens to.

resources.detail: Monthly expenses of $16,487 against savings of $412,336. 25 months runway at zero income. Formally suspending CEO salary draw pending Q2 restructure plan.

chosen_actions.reasoning: The tick 5 outcome showed savings dropping by exactly one month of expenses — the system is tracking a burn with no income. I need to own that reality explicitly rather than waiting for a recovery that may not come at the velocity required. 25 months is a real runway if I act. It is not a runway if I spend it hoping.

chosen_actions.description: Contact Angela Wright to confirm receipt of her formal progress update and to give her one additional directive: cross-reference the people I laid off this month against her transition program enrollment list. Anyone from my layoffs who has not yet enrolled — I want Angela to reach out personally, with my name behind it, and ensure they know the $2,500 grant threshold is being lowered to 10% on auto row, that First Community Bank has small-dollar loan products via David Chen, and that Millfield Community College enrollment is open. I am not managing optics. I am making sure the people I let go have a path.

resources.detail: Directive to Angela Wright to cross-reference layoffs with transition enrollment and conduct personal outreach.

chosen_actions.reasoning: Angela is the architect of the transition plan and has the institutional trust and reach to execute this. The $12,000 stay bonus I committed to her was contingent on her leading this work. This is exactly that work.

response.inner_monologue: I built this from one lot and I am not going to pretend that 'unemployed' on a status file is the end of it — but I am also not going to pretend it means nothing. The layoffs happened. The revenue is down. The showroom is not coming back the way it was, and I have known that longer than I have been willing to say. What I still have is Rick, Angela, the service lane, and 25 months to make something real out of the wreckage. My father would not have frozen. He also would not have pretended. I am going to do this the honest way — smaller, tighter, built around what actually still works — and I am going to take care of the people I let go before I take care of my own narrative.
